newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: IMPLATS ACCUSE STRIKERS OF INTIMIDATION.
newsitem.headline: IMPLATS ACCUSE STRIKERS OF INTIMIDATION.

text.p: Impala Platinum Ltd said on Wednesday said it evicted some 100 striking workers who staged a sit-in protest over pay and charged that the strikers were in violation of a court order obtained a day ago.

"Acts of intimidation, attempted assault and stone-throwing...are taking place as strikers prevent access to the works by non-striking employees. Supplier deliveries are also being refused entry," the company said in a statement late Wednesday.

Implats said its refineries' management was taking steps to try to ensure compliance with the Labour Court order it was granted on Tuesday which directed strikers not to hamper normal operations, or threaten other workers.

Implats said the strikers, who were evicted at 3pm (1300 GMT) on Wednesday, had staged their sit-in in the works premises. The strike was started on August 4 by around 400 members of the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM), out of the 1,100 workforce.
Management's last wage offer was a 10.7 percent increase, against the NUM's last demand of 19.2 percent.
The company said negotiations had resumed with union representatives, adding: "Management remains committed to a negotiated settlement."
Implats produced 499,000 ounces of refined platinum in the six months to end-December 1996.
